inventory.name: rawgamepadinputchange event on window — fires when the gamepad hardware reports new button or axis data, at the device's native polling rate independent of requestAnimationFrame
event.gamepad — a snapshot Gamepad object delivered to the listener, exposing index, buttons (GamepadButton[] with pressed/touched/value), axes (values in [-1, 1]), and timestamp

syntax.rationale: Coord ruling 2(b): the declaration grammar this page turns on is the API call form in the example block at #example — window.addEventListener('rawgamepadinputchange', (event) => { handleInput(event.gamepad); }) — not the inline <code> mentions elsewhere. The page adds no new interface: the change is a new event delivered on window.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: the #gamepad-event table lists only the event target (window), the firing condition (hardware reports new data), and the Gamepad snapshot fields, with no throwing or failure surface. The W3C Gamepad working draft (fetched 2026-10-06) does not name rawgamepadinputchange at all, and the ChromeStatus record carries no event-specific error behaviour.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: #why-it-exists motivates the event purely as a latency reduction (polling at 60 Hz vs device reports at 1000 Hz or higher), reading state that was already obtainable via navigator.getGamepads(). The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) has privacy_review_status and security_review_status both 'Pending' and an empty security_risks field, so no reviewed security/privacy consideration exists for the page to document.

syntax.rationale: The access form a reader writes to reach this snapshot is shown in the #example block: const { gamepad } = event; then gamepad.buttons[0].pressed, gamepad.axes[0], and gamepad.timestamp. That is the real declaration/access grammar, not the inline <code> field mentions in the #gamepad-event table.

errors.rationale: The #gamepad-event table documents the snapshot's fields (index, buttons, axes, timestamp) as plain reads of a Gamepad object and defines no error path: reading a field of the existing Gamepad interface has no throwing surface, and the page lists no failure mode. The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) defines none either.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The snapshot exposes button/axis/timestamp values that the existing polling Gamepad API already returned, so the page documents no new data exposure: #why-it-exists frames the change as timing (event delivery vs polling), not as a new category of information. The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) carries no reviewed security/privacy consideration for the event.

CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS — BOTH SIDES STATED, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: (1) The page's 'shape of the API' citation and #at-a-glance cite the 'W3C Gamepad spec (working draft)' as the source of the rawgamepadinputchange event and its shape, but fetched 2026-10-06 the spec at w3c.github.io/gamepad contains zero occurrences of 'rawgamepadinputchange'; its defined events are gamepadconnected/gamepaddisconnected, and its 'Other events' note lists future 'gamepadchanged'/'gamepadaxischanged' as 'more discussion needed'. The event name appears in the ChromeStatus record 5989275208253440 summary (and in the Microsoft Edge explainer, which this page does not link). (2) The page's #at-a-glance says to enable chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, but fetched 2026-10-06 the ChromeStatus record's flag_name is '#gamepad-raw-input-change-event' with flag:false. (3) The page labels the feature 'In developer trial (behind a flag)', while fetched 2026-10-06 the ChromeStatus record reads browser status 'In development' (val 3), intent_stage 'Start incubating', flag:false, origintrial:false. The page's Firefox/Safari 'No signal' and Firefox experimental-implementation note match the record's ff/safari views (fetched 2026-10-06).
